#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Secure FTPS (explicit TLS) deploy of dist/ via lftp.
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/deploy-ftp.sh            # dry run (shows what would change)
#   scripts/deploy-ftp.sh --apply    # upload for real
#   scripts/deploy-ftp.sh --apply --delete   # also remove remote files not in dist/
#
# Config (env vars, none are secrets except the password):
#   FTP_HOST        default: cricketjyvaskyla.com
#   FTP_USER        default: aksgul5
#   FTP_REMOTE_DIR  REQUIRED, e.g. /public_html
#   FTP_PASS        optional; else read from macOS Keychain item "jcc-ftp",
#                   else prompted (hidden). Never put it in a file in the repo.
#
# One-time Keychain setup:
#   security add-generic-password -a "$FTP_USER" -s jcc-ftp -w
set -euo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

HOST="${FTP_HOST:-cricketjyvaskyla.com}"
USER_NAME="${FTP_USER:-aksgul5}"
REMOTE_DIR="${FTP_REMOTE_DIR:?Set FTP_REMOTE_DIR (e.g. /public_html)}"

APPLY=0
DELETE=0
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --apply) APPLY=1 ;;
    --delete) DELETE=1 ;;
    *) echo "Unknown arg: $arg" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done

command -v lftp >/dev/null || { echo "lftp missing: brew install lftp" >&2; exit 1; }

echo "==> Building"
npm run build

[ -f dist/index.html ] || { echo "dist/index.html missing, aborting" >&2; exit 1; }

# Password: env -> Keychain -> hidden prompt
PASS="${FTP_PASS:-}"
if [ -z "$PASS" ] && command -v security >/dev/null; then
  PASS="$(security find-generic-password -a "$USER_NAME" -s jcc-ftp -w 2>/dev/null || true)"
fi
if [ -z "$PASS" ]; then
  read -r -s -p "FTP password for $USER_NAME@$HOST: " PASS
  echo
fi

OPTS="--reverse --only-newer --parallel=2 --verbose"
[ "$DELETE" -eq 1 ] && OPTS="$OPTS --delete"
[ "$APPLY" -eq 0 ] && OPTS="$OPTS --dry-run" && echo "==> DRY RUN (use --apply to upload)"

# Script goes via stdin, so the password never appears in argv / ps.
lftp <<EOF
set cmd:fail-exit yes
set ftp:ssl-force true
set ftp:ssl-protect-data true
set ftp:ssl-protect-list true
set ftp:ssl-allow no
set ssl:min-protocol TLSv1.2
set ssl:verify-certificate yes
set net:max-retries 2
set net:timeout 20
open -u "$USER_NAME","$PASS" ftp://$HOST
mirror $OPTS --exclude-glob .DS_Store dist/ "$REMOTE_DIR"
bye
EOF

echo "==> Done"

Wrote `scripts/deploy-ftp.sh`. Syntax check passes. I haven't run it against the server.

**Problem with the FileZilla config:** it uses plain FTP on port 21 (`Protocol 0`). Password and files cross the network unencrypted. The script forces **FTPS (explicit TLS)**:
- TLS is mandatory for login, data and listings. There is no fallback to plain FTP.
- The server cert is verified, with TLS 1.2 as the minimum.
- The password is never in the repo and never in `ps` output. The script looks for it in `$FTP_PASS`, then macOS Keychain, then a hidden prompt.

**Setup (one time):**
```bash
security add-generic-password -a aksgul5 -s jcc-ftp -w   # prompts for password
export FTP_REMOTE_DIR=/public_html                        # confirm real web root
```

**Use:**
```bash
scripts/deploy-ftp.sh                  # builds, then dry run
scripts/deploy-ftp.sh --apply          # uploads
scripts/deploy-ftp.sh --apply --delete # also removes remote files not in dist/
```
It uploads only newer files. `--delete` is opt-in. Check the dry run first, since the remote dir may hold other things.

**Check before trusting it:**
1. Does the host support FTPS? Try a dry run. If TLS fails, ask the host for **SFTP** (port 22). That's better still, and I can switch the script to it.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Secure FTPS (explicit TLS) deploy of dist/ via lftp.
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/deploy-ftp.sh            # dry run (shows what would change)
#   scripts/deploy-ftp.sh --apply    # upload for real
#   scripts/deploy-ftp.sh --apply --delete   # also remove remote files not in dist/
#
# Shows a single live-updating status line while running, then a summary of
# the files targeted for change. Asks for confirmation when not on master/main.
#
# Config (env vars, none are secrets except the password):
#   FTP_HOST        default: ftps4.us.freehostia.com
#   FTP_USER        default: aksgul5
#   FTP_REMOTE_DIR  REQUIRED, e.g. /public_html
#   FTP_PASS        optional; else read from macOS Keychain item "jcc-ftp",
#                   else prompted (hidden). Never put it in a file in the repo.
#
# One-time Keychain setup:
#   security add-generic-password -a "$FTP_USER" -s jcc-ftp -w
set -euo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

HOST="${FTP_HOST:-ftps4.us.freehostia.com}"
USER_NAME="${FTP_USER:-aksgul5}"
REMOTE_DIR="${FTP_REMOTE_DIR:?Set FTP_REMOTE_DIR (e.g. /public_html)}"

APPLY=0
DELETE=0
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --apply) APPLY=1 ;;
    --delete) DELETE=1 ;;
    *) echo "Unknown arg: $arg" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done

command -v lftp >/dev/null || { echo "lftp missing: brew install lftp" >&2; exit 1; }

# --- Branch guard -----------------------------------------------------------
BRANCH="$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)"
if [ "$BRANCH" != "master" ] && [ "$BRANCH" != "main" ]; then
  echo "WARNING: on branch '$BRANCH', not master/main."
  echo "         The deployed site will be built from this branch."
  ans=""
  read -r -p "Continue anyway? [y/N] " ans || true
  case "$ans" in
    y|Y|yes|YES) ;;
    *) echo "Aborted."; exit 1 ;;
  esac
fi

# --- Temp files -------------------------------------------------------------
BUILD_LOG="$(mktemp)"
ACTIONS="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$BUILD_LOG" "$ACTIONS"' EXIT

# --- Live status line -------------------------------------------------------
if [ -t 1 ]; then
  TTY=1
  COLS="$(tput cols 2>/dev/null || echo 80)"
else
  TTY=0
  COLS=80
fi

# status "text": rewrite the current line (or plain line when not a TTY)
status() {
  if [ "$TTY" -eq 1 ]; then
    local s="$1"
    [ "${#s}" -ge "$COLS" ] && s="${s:0:$((COLS - 2))}…"
    printf '\r\033[K%s' "$s"
  else
    printf '%s\n' "$1"
  fi
}
# endstatus: clear the live line
endstatus() { [ "$TTY" -eq 1 ] && printf '\r\033[K' || true; }

# --- Build ------------------------------------------------------------------
status "Building site..."
if ! npm run build >"$BUILD_LOG" 2>&1; then
  endstatus
  echo "Build failed:" >&2
  tail -n 40 "$BUILD_LOG" >&2
  exit 1
fi
endstatus
echo "Build OK (branch: $BRANCH)"

[ -f dist/index.html ] || { echo "dist/index.html missing, aborting" >&2; exit 1; }

# --- Password: env -> Keychain -> hidden prompt -----------------------------
PASS="${FTP_PASS:-}"
if [ -z "$PASS" ] && command -v security >/dev/null; then
  PASS="$(security find-generic-password -a "$USER_NAME" -s jcc-ftp -w 2>/dev/null || true)"
fi
if [ -z "$PASS" ]; then
  read -r -s -p "FTP password for $USER_NAME@$HOST: " PASS
  echo
fi

OPTS="--reverse --only-newer --parallel=2 --verbose"
[ "$DELETE" -eq 1 ] && OPTS="$OPTS --delete"
if [ "$APPLY" -eq 0 ]; then
  OPTS="$OPTS --dry-run"
  echo "DRY RUN (use --apply to upload)"
fi

# --- Run lftp, parse its output into live status + action list --------------
# Script goes via stdin, so the password never appears in argv / ps.
# lftp verbose lines parsed:
#   Transferring file `X'      -> upload X
#   Removing old file `X'      -> remove X (before overwrite, or --delete)
#   Making directory `X'       -> mkdir X
#   Removing old directory `X' -> rmdir X
set +e
lftp <<EOF 2>&1 | while IFS= read -r line; do
set cmd:fail-exit yes
set ftp:ssl-force true
set ftp:ssl-protect-data true
set ftp:ssl-protect-list true
set ftp:ssl-allow no
set ssl:verify-certificate yes
set net:max-retries 2
set net:timeout 20
status "Connecting to $HOST..."
open -u "$USER_NAME","$PASS" ftp://$HOST
mirror $OPTS --exclude-glob .DS_Store dist/ "$REMOTE_DIR"
bye
EOF
  case "$line" in
    "Transferring file \`"*)
      f="${line#*\`}"; f="${f%\'}"
      printf 'T\t%s\n' "$f" >>"$ACTIONS"
      status "$([ "$APPLY" -eq 1 ] && echo Uploading || echo Checking): $f" ;;
    "Removing old file \`"*)
      f="${line#*\`}"; f="${f%\'}"
      printf 'R\t%s\n' "$f" >>"$ACTIONS"
      status "Replacing: $f" ;;
    "Making directory \`"*)
      f="${line#*\`}"; f="${f%\'}"
      printf 'M\t%s\n' "$f" >>"$ACTIONS"
      status "Creating dir: $f" ;;
    "Removing old directory \`"*)
      f="${line#*\`}"; f="${f%\'}"
      printf 'X\t%s\n' "$f" >>"$ACTIONS"
      status "Removing dir: $f" ;;
    # dry-run echoes the underlying commands; ignore that noise
    "get "*|"put "*|"rm "*|"rmdir "*|"mkdir "*|"") ;;
    *)
      endstatus
      printf '%s\n' "$line" >&2 ;;
  esac
done
RC="${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
set -e
endstatus

if [ "$RC" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "lftp failed (exit $RC). Check output above." >&2
  exit "$RC"
fi

# --- Summary ----------------------------------------------------------------
# A file with both R and T = overwritten; T only = new; R only = deleted.
awk -F'\t' -v apply="$APPLY" '
  $1=="T" { t[$2]=1; order[++n]=$2 }
  $1=="R" { r[$2]=1; if (!($2 in seen)) { seen[$2]=1; rorder[++m]=$2 } }
  $1=="M" { dirs[++d]=$2 }
  $1=="X" { rdirs[++x]=$2 }
  END {
    for (i=1;i<=n;i++) { f=order[i]; if (f in r) upd[++u]=f; else new[++w]=f }
    for (i=1;i<=m;i++) { f=rorder[i]; if (!(f in t)) del[++k]=f }
    verb = apply ? "Changed" : "Would change"
    print ""
    print "== " verb ": " u+0 " updated, " w+0 " new, " k+0 " deleted, " d+0 " dirs created, " x+0 " dirs removed =="
    cap=100
    sec("Updated", upd, u, cap, "~")
    sec("New", new, w, cap, "+")
    sec("Deleted", del, k, cap, "-")
    sec("Dirs created", dirs, d, cap, "+")
    sec("Dirs removed", rdirs, x, cap, "-")
    if (u+w+k+d+x == 0) print "Nothing to do: remote already up to date."
  }
  function sec(title, arr, cnt, cap, mark,   i) {
    if (cnt+0 == 0) return
    print title " (" cnt "):"
    for (i=1;i<=cnt && i<=cap;i++) print "  " mark " " arr[i]
    if (cnt > cap) print "  ... and " (cnt-cap) " more"
  }
' "$ACTIONS"

[ "$APPLY" -eq 0 ] && echo && echo "Dry run only. Re-run with --apply to upload."
exit 0

#   Removing old file `X'      -> remove X (before overwrite, or --delete)
#   Making directory `X'       -> mkdir X
#   Removing old directory `X' -> rmdir X
status "Connecting to $HOST..."
set +e
lftp <<EOF 2>&1 | while IFS= read -r line; do
set cmd:fail-exit yes
set ftp:ssl-force true
set ftp:ssl-protect-data true
set ftp:ssl-protect-list true
set ftp:ssl-allow no
set ssl:verify-certificate yes
set net:max-retries 2
set net:timeout 20
open -u "$USER_NAME","$PASS" ftp://$HOST
mirror $OPTS --exclude-glob .DS_Store dist/ "$REMOTE_DIR"
bye
EOF
  case "$line" in
    "Transferring file \`"*)
      f="${line#*\`}"; f="${f%\'}"
      printf 'T\t%s\n' "$f" >>"$ACTIONS"
      status "$([ "$APPLY" -eq 1 ] && echo Uploading || echo Checking): $f" ;;
    "Removing old file \`"*)
      f="${line#*\`}"; f="${f%\'}"
      printf 'R\t%s\n' "$f" >>"$ACTIONS"
      status "Replacing: $f" ;;
    "Making directory \`"*)
      f="${line#*\`}"; f="${f%\'}"
      printf 'M\t%s\n' "$f" >>"$ACTIONS"
      status "Creating dir: $f" ;;
    "Removing old directory \`"*)
      f="${line#*\`}"; f="${f%\'}"
      printf 'X\t%s\n' "$f" >>"$ACTIONS"
      status "Removing dir: $f" ;;
    # dry-run echoes the underlying commands; ignore that noise
    "get "*|"put "*|"rm "*|"rmdir "*|"mkdir "*|"") ;;
    *)
      endstatus
      printf '%s\n' "$line" >&2 ;;
  esac
done
RC="${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
set -e
endstatus

if [ "$RC" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "lftp failed (exit $RC). Check output above." >&2
  exit "$RC"
fi

# --- Summary ----------------------------------------------------------------
# A file with both R and T = overwritten; T only = new; R only = deleted.
awk -F'\t' -v apply="$APPLY" '
  $1=="T" { t[$2]=1; order[++n]=$2 }
  $1=="R" { r[$2]=1; if (!($2 in seen)) { seen[$2]=1; rorder[++m]=$2 } }
  $1=="M" { dirs[++d]=$2 }
  $1=="X" { rdirs[++x]=$2 }
  END {
    for (i=1;i<=n;i++) { f=order[i]; if (f in r) upd[++u]=f; else new[++w]=f }
    for (i=1;i<=m;i++) { f=rorder[i]; if (!(f in t)) del[++k]=f }
    verb = apply ? "Changed" : "Would change"
    print ""
    print "== " verb ": " u+0 " updated, " w+0 " new, " k+0 " deleted, " d+0 " dirs created, " x+0 " dirs removed =="
    cap=100
    sec("Updated", upd, u, cap, "~")
    sec("New", new, w, cap, "+")
    sec("Deleted", del, k, cap, "-")
    sec("Dirs created", dirs, d, cap, "+")
    sec("Dirs removed", rdirs, x, cap, "-")
    if (u+w+k+d+x == 0) print "Nothing to do: remote already up to date."
  }
  function sec(title, arr, cnt, cap, mark,   i) {
    if (cnt+0 == 0) return
    print title " (" cnt "):"
    for (i=1;i<=cnt && i<=cap;i++) print "  " mark " " arr[i]

"""Minimal fake FTP control-channel server that logs every command a client sends.

Advertises AUTH TLS in FEAT but refuses AUTH, so we can see whether a client
falls back to sending USER/PASS in cleartext.
Usage: python3 -I fakeftp.py PORT
"""
import socket
import sys

port = int(sys.argv[1])
srv = socket.socket()
srv.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
srv.bind(("127.0.0.1", port))
srv.listen(4)
srv.settimeout(12)

for _ in range(3):
    try:
        conn, _addr = srv.accept()
    except socket.timeout:
        break
    conn.settimeout(8)
    f = conn.makefile("rwb")

    def send(x):
        f.write(x.encode() + b"\r\n")
        f.flush()

    print("--- new connection", flush=True)
    send("220 fake ftp")
    try:
        while True:
            line = f.readline()
            if not line:
                break
            cmd = line.decode(errors="replace").strip()
            print("C:", cmd, flush=True)
            verb = cmd.split(" ")[0].upper()
            if verb == "FEAT":
                f.write(b"211-Features:\r\n AUTH TLS\r\n PBSZ\r\n PROT\r\n211 End\r\n")
                f.flush()
            elif verb == "AUTH":
                send("534 TLS refused by fake server")
            elif verb == "USER":
                send("331 need password")
            elif verb == "PASS":
                send("530 login incorrect")
            elif verb == "QUIT":
                send("221 bye")
                break
            else:
                send("502 not implemented")
    except socket.timeout:
        pass
    conn.close()

* **Evidence:** I ran lftp 4.9.3 with the script's exact settings against a fake local FTP server that offers TLS.
  * The server received `FEAT`, `USER testuser`, `PASS SECRETPW123`, `PWD`, `QUIT`, and no `AUTH TLS`.
  * With `ftp:ssl-allow yes`, lftp sent `AUTH TLS`. When the server refused, it stopped with `ftp:ssl-force is set and server does not support or allow SSL`, before sending the username or password.
  * An unmodified copy of the script, run end to end, also sent `USER aksgul5` and `PASS <pw>` with no encryption.
  * With `--parallel=2`, every extra connection sends the password again.
* **Exploit scenario:** Anyone on the network path can read the password as it goes past: public Wi-Fi, a compromised router, the ISP, or the host's own network. That gives them write access to the site's folder on the server. Someone actively intercepting traffic can also change the HTML or JS while it uploads, without needing the password at all.
* **Exposure so far:** I found no sign the real password has been sent yet. Every run in your shell history used the earlier version of the script. That version stopped on the `ssl:min-protocol` error before it opened a connection. **The next run of the current script will send the password in plain text. Do not run it until this is fixed.**
* **Recommendation:** Replace the TLS settings with:
  ```
  set ftp:ssl-allow yes
  set ftp:ssl-force yes
  set ftp:ssl-auth TLS
  set ftp:ssl-protect-data yes
  set ftp:ssl-protect-list yes
  set ssl:verify-certificate yes
  set ssl:check-hostname yes
  ```
  Then re-run the fake-server test as a regression check. The script must stop with the `ssl-force` error and must never send the username or password.

---

## Below the confidence bar (7/10, not reported as a finding)

**The default dry run prints the password to the terminal** (`deploy-ftp.sh:129`, `:151`, `:154`). I tested this end to end; I'm listing it because the fix is small and the exposure is real.
* `mirror --dry-run` prints lines such as `chmod -f 644 ftp://aksgul5:<password>@host/...`.
* The output filter on line 151 doesn't drop `chmod` lines, so line 154 prints them unchanged.
* Every build gives every file a new timestamp, so every dry run prints these lines.
* The repo's Entire pre-push hook pushes AI session transcripts to `origin`, and the repo is public. If the dry run is ever run through an agent's shell tool, the password could end up published. No real password has leaked so far.

The fix:
1. Use `open --env-password -u "$USER_NAME" ftp://$HOST` and run lftp as `LFTP_PASSWORD="$PASS" lftp ...`. The dry-run lines then show no password. This also keeps the password out of the lftp command text, so a `"` in it can no longer break the quoting or inject lftp commands.
2. Add `"chmod "*` to the filter on line 151.

---

## If the FTP password is compromised: impact and mitigations

**What an attacker gets.** Full write and delete access to the site's folder on Freehostia. This matters only if the domain's DNS actually points at Freehostia; CLAUDE.md says the site is on Netlify. With that access they can:
* Change payment or contact details in pages and PDFs (fees, expense form, by-laws, signed letters) to phish members on a domain they trust.
* Inject scripts for card skimming, redirects or spam, which can get the domain blocklisted by browsers.
* Probably upload a PHP webshell, since Freehostia shared hosting normally runs PHP. I have not verified this for your plan. That would give code execution as the hosting account.

**Redeploying won't clean it up.** By default the script only uploads files that are newer and never deletes anything (`--only-newer`, no `--delete`). So an attacker's added files survive every normal deploy, such as a webshell, a phishing page or an `.htaccess` redirect. A tampered file with a future timestamp is also skipped.

**Possible account takeover.** `aksgul5` looks like the main hosting login. If the same password opens the Freehostia control panel, an attacker could also take over DNS, mail and the domain itself.

**Mitigations:**
1. Fix Vuln 1, and the dry-run leak above, before the next run.
2. Use a dedicated FTP sub-account limited to the web folder, with a unique password.
3. If any version without the `ssl:min-protocol` line has ever reached the real host, change the password.
4. After a suspected compromise:
   * Change the password.
   * Check `.htaccess`, hidden files, and anything outside the web folder.
   * Do a full re-upload with `--apply --delete` and without `--only-newer`.
5. Every so often, run a `--delete` dry run to spot remote files that aren't in `dist/`.

**Hardening notes (not findings):**
* **Keychain item readable by any of your processes.** The setup command creates the item without `-T`, so any process running as you can read it without a prompt. Recreate it with `-T ""` so every read asks first.
* **`FTP_PASS` passed to the build.** If set, it is inherited by `npm run build` and every build process. Clear it before the build runs.
* **Netlify headers skipped.** A Freehostia deploy doesn't get the security headers or redirects in `netlify.toml`.
* **A passing dry run doesn't prove login or TLS worked.** It can show a plan even when the login failed.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Offline regression test for scripts/deploy-ftp.sh security guarantees.
# Runs the real deploy script against a local fake FTP server (no network,
# no real credentials) and asserts that the password is never sent or printed:
#
#   1. Server without TLS          -> script aborts, server never sees USER/PASS
#   2. Server with untrusted cert  -> script aborts, server never sees USER/PASS
#
# Usage: scripts/test-deploy-ftp.sh      (needs python3, lftp, openssl, dist/)
set -uo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

[ -f dist/index.html ] || { echo "Run 'npm run build' once first (dist/ missing)." >&2; exit 2; }
for bin in python3 lftp openssl; do
  command -v "$bin" >/dev/null || { echo "Missing: $bin" >&2; exit 2; }
done

WORK="$(mktemp -d)"
SRV_PID=""
cleanup() { [ -n "$SRV_PID" ] && kill "$SRV_PID" 2>/dev/null; rm -rf "$WORK"; }
trap cleanup EXIT

FAKE_PW="REDACTED"   # fake value; must never show up anywhere

# Stub npm so the test does not rebuild the site.
mkdir -p "$WORK/bin"
printf '#!/bin/sh\nexit 0\n' >"$WORK/bin/npm"
chmod +x "$WORK/bin/npm"

# Self-signed cert for test 2 (not trusted by the system CA store).
openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -days 1 -subj "/CN=127.0.0.1" \
  -keyout "$WORK/key.pem" -out "$WORK/cert.pem" >/dev/null 2>&1

cat >"$WORK/fakeftp.py" <<'PY'
import socket, ssl, sys
mode, portfile, logfile, certdir = sys.argv[1:5]
log = open(logfile, "a", buffering=1)
srv = socket.socket()
srv.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
srv.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
srv.listen(4)
srv.settimeout(20)
open(portfile, "w").write(str(srv.getsockname()[1]))
ctx = ssl.SSLContext(ssl.PROTOCOL_TLS_SERVER)
ctx.load_cert_chain(certdir + "/cert.pem", certdir + "/key.pem")
while True:
    try:
        conn, _ = srv.accept()
    except socket.timeout:
        break
    conn.settimeout(10)
    f = conn.makefile("rwb", buffering=0)
    send = lambda s: f.write((s + "\r\n").encode())
    send("220 fake")
    try:
        while True:
            line = f.readline()
            if not line:
                break
            cmd = line.decode(errors="replace").strip()
            log.write("C: " + cmd + "\n")
            verb = cmd.split(" ")[0].upper()
            if verb == "FEAT":
                f.write(b"211-Features:\r\n AUTH TLS\r\n PBSZ\r\n PROT\r\n211 End\r\n")
            elif verb == "AUTH" and mode == "notls":
                send("534 TLS refused")
            elif verb == "AUTH" and mode == "selfsigned":
                send("234 go ahead")
                try:
                    conn = ctx.wrap_socket(conn, server_side=True)
                    f = conn.makefile("rwb", buffering=0)
                    send = lambda s: f.write((s + "\r\n").encode())
                    log.write("TLS handshake completed\n")
                except Exception as e:
                    log.write("TLS handshake rejected by client: %s\n" % e)
                    break
            elif verb == "USER":
                send("331 need password")
            elif verb == "PASS":
                send("530 login incorrect")
            elif verb == "QUIT":
                send("221 bye")
                break
            else:
                send("502 not implemented")
    except Exception:
        pass
    conn.close()
PY

FAILS=0
check() { # check "description" condition-exit-code
  if [ "$2" -eq 0 ]; then echo "  PASS  $1"; else echo "  FAIL  $1"; FAILS=$((FAILS + 1)); fi
}

run_case() { # run_case mode title
  local mode="$1" title="$2"
  local portfile="$WORK/port.$mode" srvlog="$WORK/srv.$mode.log" out="$WORK/out.$mode.log"
  : >"$srvlog"
  python3 -I "$WORK/fakeftp.py" "$mode" "$portfile" "$srvlog" "$WORK" &
  SRV_PID=$!
  for _ in $(seq 50); do [ -s "$portfile" ] && break; sleep 0.1; done
  local port; port="$(cat "$portfile")"

  echo "== $title"
  # "y" answers the branch guard if not on master/main.
  echo y | PATH="$WORK/bin:$PATH" FTP_HOST="127.0.0.1:$port" FTP_USER=testuser \
    FTP_PASS="$FAKE_PW" FTP_REMOTE_DIR=/www scripts/deploy-ftp.sh >"$out" 2>&1
  local rc=$?
  kill "$SRV_PID" 2>/dev/null; wait "$SRV_PID" 2>/dev/null; SRV_PID=""

  [ "$rc" -ne 0 ];                                  check "deploy script exits non-zero (rc=$rc)" $?
  grep -q '^C: AUTH TLS' "$srvlog";                 check "client asked for TLS (AUTH TLS)" $?
  ! grep -qE '^C: (USER|PASS)' "$srvlog";           check "server never received USER/PASS" $?
  ! grep -qF "$FAKE_PW" "$srvlog" "$out";           check "password not in server log or script output" $?
  if [ "$FAILS" -gt 0 ]; then
    echo "  --- server log:";  sed 's/^/    /' "$srvlog"
    echo "  --- script output:"; sed 's/^/    /' "$out"
  fi
}

run_case notls      "Server refuses TLS"
run_case selfsigned "Server presents an untrusted certificate"

echo
if [ "$FAILS" -eq 0 ]; then echo "All checks passed."; else echo "$FAILS check(s) FAILED."; exit 1; fi

I've fixed `scripts/deploy-ftp.sh` and added an offline test for it, `scripts/test-deploy-ftp.sh`. All checks pass. Nothing is committed yet.

## Fixes

| # | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **TLS was off, so the password went out in plain text** | `ftp:ssl-allow yes` with `ssl-force yes`, `ssl-auth TLS` and `ssl:check-hostname yes`. lftp now refuses to log in unless TLS works. |
| 2 | **The dry run printed the password in `chmod` lines** | The password now reaches lftp through the `LFTP_PASSWORD` environment variable (`open --env-password`), so it no longer appears in lftp's URLs or command text. `chmod` lines are now filtered, and any other output has `user:pass@` replaced with `user:***@`. |
| 3 | `FTP_PASS` was passed on to `npm run build` | The script saves it and removes it from the environment before the build runs. |
| 4 | Any program running as you could read the Keychain item without asking | The setup steps now create it with `-T ""`, so every read shows a macOS approval dialog. |
| 5 | A dry run could "succeed" even with a wrong password | The script now changes into the remote folder before mirroring. A bad login, failed TLS or missing folder fails straight away. |
| 6 | lftp could send commands without waiting for replies | `ftp:sync-mode yes`, so lftp always waits for the server's reply before sending the password. |

## What I verified

- **Offline test:** the deploy script runs against a fake local FTP server.
  - Server refuses TLS: the script stops and the server never receives the username or password.
  - Server presents a self-signed certificate: the script stops with "Certificate verification: self-signed" and the password is never sent.
  - In that second case lftp sends the username over TLS before it rejects the certificate. The username isn't secret, but the test checks it explicitly.
- **`--env-password`:** in a side-by-side test, the old method printed `REDACTED` in the dry run and the new one prints `ftp://u@...`. The server still received the password, so login works.
- **Real host certificate**, checked with `openssl s_client` (handshake only, no login): a valid Let's Encrypt certificate for `*.us.freehostia.com`, TLS 1.3, verify code 0. lftp's certificate check should therefore pass.
- **Not yet verified:** an actual login and upload to Freehostia. That needs your password.

## How to test

**1. Offline test.** No network or real password needed. Run it after any change to the deploy script:
```bash
npm run build                 # once, if dist/ is missing
scripts/test-deploy-ftp.sh    # expect: "All checks passed."
```

**2. Put the password in the Keychain** with the stricter access setting:
```bash
security delete-generic-password -a aksgul5 -s jcc-ftp 2>/dev/null
security add-generic-password -a aksgul5 -s jcc-ftp -T "" -w
```
Each run then shows a macOS dialog. Click **Allow**, never **Always Allow**.

**3. Check the real host's certificate** (no password sent):
```bash
echo | openssl s_client -starttls ftp -connect ftps4.us.freehostia.com:21 \
  -servername ftps4.us.freehostia.com -verify_hostname ftps4.us.freehostia.com 2>&1 | grep 'Verify return code'
# expect: Verify return code: 0 (ok)
```

**4. Real dry run.** Run it in your own terminal, not through Claude: anything run through Claude ends up in session transcripts, which Entire pushes to the repo.
```bash
export FTP_REMOTE_DIR=/www    # your shell history used /www; confirm it in FileZilla
scripts/deploy-ftp.sh
```
Expect a single updating status line, then the summary block. Errors such as `Login failed` or `Certificate verification` mean it stopped safely before sending the password. Paste the error here rather than loosening any setting.

**5. Upload for real:** `scripts/deploy-ftp.sh --apply`. Add `--delete` only after the dry run with `--delete` shows the expected deletions.

**Also:** in FileZilla, switch the saved site to host `ftps4.us.freehostia.com` with "Require explicit FTP over TLS". Otherwise FileZilla still sends the password in plain text.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Upload dist/ to the web host over FTPS (FTP over TLS, certificate verified).
# Plain FTP is refused: TLS is forced on both the control and data channels.
#
# Usage: npm run deploy:ftps [-- --dry-run] [-- --delete] [-- --skip-build]
#   --dry-run     show what would change, upload nothing
#   --delete      also remove remote files that are not in dist/ (off by default)
#   --skip-build  upload the existing dist/ without rebuilding
#
# Config (host, user, paths) comes from .env.deploy (gitignored, see .env.deploy.example).
# The password is never stored in a file: it is read from the macOS Keychain
# (security add-generic-password -s jcc-ftps -a "$FTP_USER" -w) or, for CI, from $FTP_PASSWORD.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
DRY_RUN=0; DELETE=0; BUILD=1
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
    --delete) DELETE=1 ;;
    --skip-build) BUILD=0 ;;
    *) echo "Unknown option: $arg" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done
command -v lftp >/dev/null || { echo "lftp not found. Install it: brew install lftp" >&2; exit 1; }
ENV_FILE=".env.deploy"
[ -f "$ENV_FILE" ] || { echo "Missing $ENV_FILE (copy .env.deploy.example)" >&2; exit 1; }
# Refuse a config file other users can read.
if [ -n "$(find "$ENV_FILE" -perm -044 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
  echo "$ENV_FILE is readable by others. Run: chmod 600 $ENV_FILE" >&2; exit 1
fi
# shellcheck disable=SC1090
set -a; . "./$ENV_FILE"; set +a
: "${FTP_HOST:?FTP_HOST not set in $ENV_FILE}"
: "${FTP_USER:?FTP_USER not set in $ENV_FILE}"
: "${FTP_REMOTE_DIR:?FTP_REMOTE_DIR not set in $ENV_FILE}"
FTP_PORT="${FTP_PORT:-21}"
if [ -z "${FTP_PASSWORD:-}" ]; then
  FTP_PASSWORD="$(security find-generic-password -s jcc-ftps -a "$FTP_USER" -w 2>/dev/null || true)"
fi
[ -n "$FTP_PASSWORD" ] || {
  echo "No password found. Store it in the Keychain:" >&2
  echo "  security add-generic-password -s jcc-ftps -a \"$FTP_USER\" -w" >&2
  exit 1
}
if [ "$BUILD" -eq 1 ]; then npm run build; fi
[ -f dist/index.html ] || { echo "dist/index.html missing: build first" >&2; exit 1; }
MIRROR_OPTS=(--reverse --only-newer --verbose --parallel=2 --exclude-glob .DS_Store)
[ "$DELETE" -eq 1 ] && MIRROR_OPTS+=(--delete)
[ "$DRY_RUN" -eq 1 ] && MIRROR_OPTS+=(--dry-run)
# Commands (including the password) go over stdin, not argv, so they stay out of `ps`.
lftp <<LFTP
set cmd:fail-exit yes
set ftp:ssl-force true
set ftp:ssl-protect-data true
set ftp:ssl-allow true
set ftp:ssl-auth TLS
set ssl:verify-certificate yes
set ssl:min-protocol TLSv1.2
set ftp:passive-mode true
set net:max-retries 2

gh pr create --base master --head feat/secure-ftp-deploy --title "feat: Add secured FTPS deploy script with offline regression test" --body-file - <<'EOF'
## Summary

Adds an alternative deploy path that uploads `dist/` to the Freehostia web host over **explicit FTPS** with lftp. It replaces plain-FTP uploads from FileZilla, which send the password unencrypted. Netlify deployment is unchanged.

- `scripts/deploy-ftp.sh`: builds, then mirrors `dist/` to `FTP_REMOTE_DIR`
  - **TLS mandatory** (`ftp:ssl-allow` + `ftp:ssl-force`), with certificate and hostname verification. lftp aborts before sending the password if any of this fails.
  - **Password handling**: taken from `FTP_PASS`, the macOS Keychain (`-T ""`, so every read needs approval) or a hidden prompt. It reaches lftp only through `LFTP_PASSWORD` / `open --env-password`, so it never appears in argv, the lftp command text, or the URLs lftp prints. `FTP_PASS` is unset before `npm run build`. Unrecognised lftp output is scrubbed of `user:pass@`.
  - **The FTP login is not hardcoded** because this repo is public. `FTP_USER` and `FTP_REMOTE_DIR` are required.
  - **UX**: dry run by default, a single live-updating status line, and an end summary of files that are updated, new or deleted and directories touched. It asks for confirmation when not on `master`/`main`. `--delete` is opt-in.
- `scripts/test-deploy-ftp.sh`: an offline regression test that runs the real script against a local fake FTP server.
- `DEPLOYMENT.md`: setup and usage for the script.

## Security notes

A security review of the first version found two real issues. Both are fixed here, and no real credentials had been sent yet.
1. `ftp:ssl-allow no` disabled TLS entirely, so `ssl-force` was never consulted and USER/PASS went out in cleartext. Confirmed against a fake server.
2. The default dry run printed `chmod … REDACTED` lines, which leaked the password to the terminal.

Also checked: the renamed PDF and the content changes on the role-changes branch were clean, and no credentials are committed anywhere in the history.

## Test plan

- [x] `scripts/test-deploy-ftp.sh` passes all checks. Server refuses TLS: no USER/PASS sent. Untrusted certificate: no PASS sent. The password never appears in output.
- [x] With `--env-password`, dry-run URLs show `ftp://user@host/…` and the server still receives PASS.
- [x] Real host certificate checked with `openssl s_client -starttls ftp` (no login): Let's Encrypt, `*.us.freehostia.com`, TLS 1.3, verify OK.
- [x] A real login over TLS succeeded: the run failed afterwards at `cd /www` with 550, which means TLS and authentication worked.
- [ ] Confirm the correct `FTP_REMOTE_DIR`, then run the dry run and `--apply` from `master`, in your own terminal rather than through an agent shell.
- [ ] Switch the FileZilla site to "Require explicit FTP over TLS".

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Secure FTPS (explicit TLS) deploy of dist/ via lftp.
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/deploy-ftp.sh            # dry run (shows what would change)
#   scripts/deploy-ftp.sh --apply    # upload for real
#   scripts/deploy-ftp.sh --apply --delete   # also remove remote files not in dist/
#   scripts/deploy-ftp.sh --full ... # ignore the record of the last deploy and
#                                    # treat every file as changed
#
# Shows a single live-updating status line while running, then a summary of
# the files targeted for change. Asks for confirmation when not on master/main.
#
# Config (env vars, none are secrets except the password):
#   FTP_HOST        default: ftps4.us.freehostia.com
#   FTP_USER        REQUIRED, your FTP login (kept out of the repo on purpose)
#   FTP_REMOTE_DIR  REQUIRED, e.g. /public_html
#   FTP_PASS        optional; else read from macOS Keychain item "jcc-ftp",
#                   else prompted (hidden). Never put it in a file in the repo.
#
# One-time Keychain setup. -T "" trusts no app, so every read must be approved
# in a macOS dialog (choose "Allow", never "Always Allow"):
#   security delete-generic-password -a "$FTP_USER" -s jcc-ftp 2>/dev/null
#   security add-generic-password -a "$FTP_USER" -s jcc-ftp -T "" -w
#
# Security model:
#   - TLS is mandatory (ftp:ssl-force): lftp aborts before sending the
#     password if the server will not negotiate TLS or its certificate/hostname
#     fails verification.
#   - Data connections must be encrypted too. lftp silently falls back to
#     cleartext data if the server rejects PROT P, so a preflight session
#     (login only, no data connection) checks that PROT P was accepted before
#     anything is listed or uploaded.
#   - Password reaches lftp only via LFTP_PASSWORD (open --env-password), so it
#     is not in argv, not in the lftp command text, and not in lftp's URLs.
#   - FTP_PASS is removed from the environment before `npm run build`.
#   - Any unrecognised lftp output is scrubbed of user:pass@ before printing.
#   Run scripts/test-deploy-ftp.sh after changing this script.
set -euo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

HOST="${FTP_HOST:-ftps4.us.freehostia.com}"
USER_NAME="${FTP_USER:?Set FTP_USER (your FTP login)}"
REMOTE_DIR="${FTP_REMOTE_DIR:?Set FTP_REMOTE_DIR (e.g. /public_html)}"

# Take the password out of the environment now, so the build's child
# processes (Astro, plugins, npm deps) never inherit it.
PASS="${FTP_PASS:-}"
unset FTP_PASS

APPLY=0
DELETE=0
FULL=0
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --apply) APPLY=1 ;;
    --delete) DELETE=1 ;;
    --full) FULL=1 ;;
    *) echo "Unknown arg: $arg" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done

command -v lftp >/dev/null || { echo "lftp missing: brew install lftp" >&2; exit 1; }
command -v node >/dev/null || { echo "node missing" >&2; exit 1; }

# --- Branch guard -----------------------------------------------------------
BRANCH="$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)"
if [ "$BRANCH" != "master" ] && [ "$BRANCH" != "main" ]; then
  echo "WARNING: on branch '$BRANCH', not master/main."
  echo "         The deployed site will be built from this branch."
  ans=""
  read -r -p "Continue anyway? [y/N] " ans || true
  case "$ans" in
    y|Y|yes|YES) ;;
    *) echo "Aborted."; exit 1 ;;
  esac
fi

# --- Temp files -------------------------------------------------------------
BUILD_LOG="$(mktemp)"
ACTIONS="$(mktemp)"
PRE_OUT="$(mktemp)"
PRE_DEBUG="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$BUILD_LOG" "$ACTIONS" "$PRE_OUT" "$PRE_DEBUG"' EXIT

# Record of the last successful deploy to this host + directory (gitignored,
# lives under node_modules/.cache). See scripts/deploy-ftp-state.mjs.
STATE_FILE="node_modules/.cache/deploy-ftp/$(printf '%s' "$HOST$REMOTE_DIR" | tr -c 'A-Za-z0-9._-' '_').json"

# --- Live status line -------------------------------------------------------
if [ -t 1 ]; then
  TTY=1
  COLS="$(tput cols 2>/dev/null || echo 80)"
else
  TTY=0
  COLS=80
fi

# status "text": rewrite the current line (or plain line when not a TTY)
status() {
  if [ "$TTY" -eq 1 ]; then
    local s="$1"
    [ "${#s}" -ge "$COLS" ] && s="${s:0:$((COLS - 2))}…"
    printf '\r\033[K%s' "$s"
  else
    printf '%s\n' "$1"
  fi
}
# endstatus: clear the live line
endstatus() { [ "$TTY" -eq 1 ] && printf '\r\033[K' || true; }

# redact: strip credentials from any ftp(s)://user:pass@ URL in a line
redact() {
  printf '%s\n' "$1" | sed -E 's#(ftps?://[^/:@[:space:]]*):[^@[:space:]]*@#\1:***@#g'
}

# --- Build ------------------------------------------------------------------
status "Building site..."
if ! npm run build >"$BUILD_LOG" 2>&1; then
  endstatus
  echo "Build failed:" >&2
  tail -n 40 "$BUILD_LOG" >&2
  exit 1
fi
endstatus
echo "Build OK (branch: $BRANCH)"

[ -f dist/index.html ] || { echo "dist/index.html missing, aborting" >&2; exit 1; }

# Give unchanged files back the mtime they had at the last deploy, so
# --only-newer uploads only what actually changed.
if [ "$FULL" -eq 1 ]; then
  echo "--full: treating every file as changed."
else
  node scripts/deploy-ftp-state.mjs restore dist "$STATE_FILE"
fi

# --- Password: env (captured above) -> Keychain -> hidden prompt -------------
if [ -z "$PASS" ] && command -v security >/dev/null; then
  PASS="$(security find-generic-password -a "$USER_NAME" -s jcc-ftp -w 2>/dev/null || true)"
fi
if [ -z "$PASS" ]; then
  read -r -s -p "FTP password for $USER_NAME@$HOST: " PASS
  echo
fi

# --- lftp environment -------------------------------------------------------
# The output parser below matches lftp's English messages, so force English
# messages without changing the character set used for file names.
LFTP_CTYPE="${LC_ALL:-${LC_CTYPE:-${LANG:-}}}"

# Settings shared by both lftp sessions. No secrets in here.
LFTP_SETTINGS="set cmd:fail-exit yes
set ftp:ssl-allow yes
set ftp:ssl-force yes
set ftp:ssl-auth TLS
set ftp:ssl-protect-data yes
set ftp:ssl-protect-list yes
set ssl:verify-certificate yes
set ssl:check-hostname yes
set ftp:sync-mode yes
set net:max-retries 2
set net:timeout 20"

# --- Preflight: login over TLS, check PROT P was accepted, check the dir -----
# lftp sends PROT P during login (protect-data and protect-list are both on),
# so this session never opens a data connection. The debug log masks the
# password ("PASS XXXX"); it is a private temp file removed on exit.
status "Checking TLS on $HOST..."
set +e
LC_ALL= LANGUAGE= LC_MESSAGES=C LC_CTYPE="$LFTP_CTYPE" LFTP_PASSWORD="$PASS" \
  lftp >"$PRE_OUT" 2>&1 <<EOF
$LFTP_SETTINGS
debug -o "$PRE_DEBUG" 9
open --env-password -u "$USER_NAME" ftp://$HOST
cd "$REMOTE_DIR"
bye
EOF
PRE_RC=$?
set -e
endstatus
if [ "$PRE_RC" -ne 0 ]; then
  while IFS= read -r line; do redact "$line" >&2; done <"$PRE_OUT"
  echo "Could not log in over TLS or open $REMOTE_DIR (lftp exit $PRE_RC). Nothing was uploaded." >&2
  exit 1
fi
# Every PROT P must be answered with 2xx, and there must be at least one.
if ! awk '
  /---> PROT P/ { want = 1; seen = 1; next }
  want && /<--- / { if ($0 !~ /<--- 2[0-9][0-9]/) bad = 1; want = 0 }
  END { exit (seen && !bad) ? 0 : 1 }
' "$PRE_DEBUG"; then
  echo "The server did not accept PROT P, so data connections would not be encrypted." >&2
  echo "Refusing to list or upload anything. Nothing was uploaded." >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "TLS OK: login and data connections encrypted, $REMOTE_DIR exists."

OPTS="--reverse --only-newer --parallel=2 --verbose"
[ "$DELETE" -eq 1 ] && OPTS="$OPTS --delete"
if [ "$APPLY" -eq 0 ]; then
  OPTS="$OPTS --dry-run"
  echo "DRY RUN (use --apply to upload)"
fi

# --- Run lftp, parse its output into live status + action list --------------
# The password is handed over in LFTP_PASSWORD (read by open --env-password);
# it is never part of argv, the lftp script text, or the session URL.
# lftp verbose lines parsed (printed in both dry-run and apply mode):
#   Transferring file `X'      -> upload X
#   Removing old file `X'      -> remove X (before an overwrite, or --delete)
#   Making directory `X'       -> mkdir X
#   Removing old directory `X' -> rmdir X
status "Comparing with $HOST..."
set +e
LC_ALL= LANGUAGE= LC_MESSAGES=C LC_CTYPE="$LFTP_CTYPE" LFTP_PASSWORD="$PASS" \
  lftp <<EOF 2>&1 | while IFS= read -r line; do
$LFTP_SETTINGS
open --env-password -u "$USER_NAME" ftp://$HOST
cd "$REMOTE_DIR"
mirror $OPTS --exclude-glob .DS_Store dist/ .
bye
EOF
  case "$line" in
    "Transferring file \`"*)
      f="${line#*\`}"; f="${f%\'}"
      printf 'T\t%s\n' "$f" >>"$ACTIONS"
      status "$([ "$APPLY" -eq 1 ] && echo Uploading || echo Checking): $f" ;;
    "Removing old file \`"*)
      f="${line#*\`}"; f="${f%\'}"
      printf 'R\t%s\n' "$f" >>"$ACTIONS"
      status "Replacing: $f" ;;
    "Making directory \`"*)
      f="${line#*\`}"; f="${f%\'}"
      printf 'M\t%s\n' "$f" >>"$ACTIONS"
      status "Creating dir: $f" ;;
    "Removing old directory \`"*)
      f="${line#*\`}"; f="${f%\'}"
      printf 'X\t%s\n' "$f" >>"$ACTIONS"
      status "Removing dir: $f" ;;
    # dry-run also echoes the underlying commands; the lines above cover them
    "get "*|"put "*|"rm "*|"rmdir "*|"mkdir "*|"chmod "*|"") ;;
    *)
      endstatus
      redact "$line" >&2 ;;
  esac
done
RC="${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
set -e
endstatus

if [ "$RC" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "lftp failed (exit $RC). Check output above." >&2
  exit "$RC"
fi

# Remember what is now on the server, so the next deploy skips unchanged files.
# Only after a fully successful upload: a failed or partial run keeps the
# previous record, so its files are compared again next time.
[ "$APPLY" -eq 1 ] && node scripts/deploy-ftp-state.mjs save dist "$STATE_FILE"

# --- Summary ----------------------------------------------------------------
# A file with both R and T = overwritten; T only = new; R only = deleted.
awk -F'\t' -v apply="$APPLY" '
  $1=="T" { t[$2]=1; order[++n]=$2 }
  $1=="R" { r[$2]=1; if (!($2 in seen)) { seen[$2]=1; rorder[++m]=$2 } }
  $1=="M" { dirs[++d]=$2 }
  $1=="X" { rdirs[++x]=$2 }
  END {
    for (i=1;i<=n;i++) { f=order[i]; if (f in r) upd[++u]=f; else new[++w]=f }
    for (i=1;i<=m;i++) { f=rorder[i]; if (!(f in t)) del[++k]=f }
    verb = apply ? "Changed" : "Would change"
    print ""
    print "== " verb ": " u+0 " updated, " w+0 " new, " k+0 " deleted, " d+0 " dirs created, " x+0 " dirs removed =="
    cap=100
    sec("Updated", upd, u, cap, "~")
    sec("New", new, w, cap, "+")
    sec("Deleted", del, k, cap, "-")
    sec("Dirs created", dirs, d, cap, "+")
    sec("Dirs removed", rdirs, x, cap, "-")
    if (u+w+k+d+x == 0) print "Nothing to do: remote already up to date."
  }
  function sec(title, arr, cnt, cap, mark,   i) {
    if (cnt+0 == 0) return
    print title " (" cnt "):"
    for (i=1;i<=cnt && i<=cap;i++) print "  " mark " " arr[i]
    if (cnt > cap) print "  ... and " (cnt-cap) " more"
  }
' "$ACTIONS"

[ "$APPLY" -eq 0 ] && echo && echo "Dry run only. Re-run with --apply to upload."
exit 0

#!/usr/bin/env bash # Offline end-to-end test for scripts/deploy-ftp.sh. # # Runs a copy of the real deploy script (in a throwaway fake repo with a small # synthetic dist/) against scripts/fake_ftps_server.py: a local FTPS server # with TLS on control and data channels, signed by a throwaway test CA. No # network, no real credentials, the real dist/ is never touched. # # Refusal cases (nothing may be uploaded, the password must not be sent): # - server refuses TLS # - server certificate not trusted # - server rejects PROT P (data connections would be cleartext) # - wrong password # Success cases (summary and server state must match): # - dry run, dry run --delete, apply, no-op re-run after a rebuild, # single changed file, German locale, --full # # Usage: scripts/test-deploy-ftp.sh (needs python3, lftp, openssl, node) set -uo pipefail REPO="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)" for bin in python3 lftp openssl node; do command -v "$bin" >/dev/null || { echo "Missing: $bin" >&2; exit 2; } done WORK="$(mktemp -d)" SRV_PID="" stop_server() { if [ -n "$SRV_PID" ]; then kill "$SRV_PID" 2>/dev/null; wait "$SRV_PID" 2>/dev/null; fi SRV_PID="" } cleanup() { stop_server; [ -n "${WORK:-}" ] && [ -d "$WORK" ] && rm -rf -- "$WORK"; } trap cleanup EXIT FAKE_PW="REDACTED" # fake value; must never show up in any output # --- Test CA + server certificate for "localhost" --------------------------- mkdir -p "$WORK/certs" ( cd "$WORK/certs" || exit 1 openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -days 1 -subj "/CN=deploy-ftp test CA" \ -addext basicConstraints=critical,CA:TRUE -addext keyUsage=critical,keyCertSign,cRLSign \ -keyout ca.key -out ca.pem openssl req -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -subj "/CN=localhost" -keyout key.pem -out srv.csr printf 'subjectAltName=DNS:localhost\nbasicConstraints=CA:FALSE\nextendedKeyUsage=serverAuth\n' >ext.cnf openssl x509 -req -in srv.csr -CA ca.pem -CAkey ca.key -CAcreateserial -days 1 -extfile ext.cnf -out cert.pem ) >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Could not create test certificates" >&2; exit 2; } # lftp reads $LFTP_HOME/rc. One home trusts the test CA, one does not. mkdir -p "$WORK/home-trust" "$WORK/home-notrust" printf 'set ssl:ca-file "%s"\nset dns:order inet\n' "$WORK/certs/ca.pem" >"$WORK/home-trust/rc" printf 'set dns:order inet\n' >"$WORK/home-notrust/rc" # --- Fake repo: copy of the deploy script + synthetic dist/ ----------------- FAKE="$WORK/repo" mkdir -p "$FAKE/scripts" "$FAKE/dist/css" "$FAKE/dist/images" "$FAKE/dist/pdfs" "$WORK/bin" cp "$REPO/scripts/deploy-ftp.sh" "$REPO/scripts/deploy-ftp-state.mjs" "$FAKE/scripts/" printf '

JCC

\n' >"$FAKE/dist/index.html" printf 'body { color: navy; }\n' >"$FAKE/dist/css/site.css" head -c 4096 /dev/urandom >"$FAKE/dist/images/logo.png" head -c 8192 /dev/urandom >"$FAKE/dist/pdfs/agm.pdf" printf 'Jyväskylä\n' >"$FAKE/dist/jyväskylä.txt" find "$FAKE/dist" -type f -exec touch -t 202001010000 {} + rebuild() { find "$FAKE/dist" -type f -exec touch {} +; } # Astro rewrites every file # Stub npm so "npm run build" is a no-op. printf '#!/bin/sh\nexit 0\n' >"$WORK/bin/npm" chmod +x "$WORK/bin/npm" # --- Helpers ---------------------------------------------------------------- STATE=""; PORT=""; OUT=""; RC=0; RUN=0 FAILS=0; CASE_FAILS=0 start_server() { # start_server MODE [seed-json] STATE="$(mktemp -d "$WORK/state.XXXX")" [ -n "${2:-}" ] && printf '%s' "$2" >"$STATE/seed.json" python3 -I "$REPO/scripts/fake_ftps_server.py" "$1" "$WORK/certs" "$STATE" "$FAKE_PW" \ 2>>"$STATE/stderr" & SRV_PID=$! for _ in $(seq 100); do [ -s "$STATE/port" ] && break; sleep 0.05; done PORT="$(cat "$STATE/port")" } # deploy LFTP_HOME [deploy-ftp.sh args...]; sets OUT (output file) and RC. # T_PASS / T_LC_ALL / T_LANG override the password and locale for one run. deploy() { local home="$1"; shift RUN=$((RUN + 1)); OUT="$WORK/out.$RUN" # "y" answers the branch guard (the fake repo is not a git checkout). echo y | PATH="$WORK/bin:$PATH" LFTP_HOME="$home" FTP_HOST="localhost:$PORT" FTP_USER=tester \ FTP_PASS="${T_PASS:-$FAKE_PW}" FTP_REMOTE_DIR=/www LC_ALL="${T_LC_ALL:-}" LANG="${T_LANG:-${LANG:-}}" \ "$FAKE/scripts/deploy-ftp.sh" "$@" >"$OUT" 2>&1 RC=$? } begin() { echo "== $1"; CASE_FAILS=0; } check() { # check "description" command... local desc="$1"; shift if "$@"; then echo " PASS $desc"; else echo " FAIL $desc"; FAILS=$((FAILS + 1)); CASE_FAILS=$((CASE_FAILS + 1)); fi } end() { if [ "$CASE_FAILS" -gt 0 ]; then echo " --- server log:"; sed 's/^/ /' "$STATE/log" echo " --- script output:"; sed 's/^/ /' "$OUT" fi } failed() { [ "$RC" -ne 0 ]; } succeeded() { [ "$RC" -eq 0 ]; } out_has() { grep -qF -- "$1" "$OUT"; } log_has() { grep -qE -- "$1" "$STATE/log"; } log_lacks() { ! grep -qE -- "$1" "$STATE/log"; } pw_hidden() { ! grep -qF -- "$FAKE_PW" "$OUT" "$STATE/log"; } stor_count() { grep -c '^C: STOR ' "$STATE/log"; } # Only FEAT and AUTH TLS may happen before TLS; every data connection is TLS. all_encrypted() { ! grep -E '^C: ' "$STATE/log" | grep ' tls=0$' | grep -qvE '^C: (FEAT|AUTH TLS) ' && ! grep -qE '^DATA .* tls=0$' "$STATE/log" } remote_has() { python3 -I -c 'import json,sys; fs=json.load(open(sys.argv[1])); sys.exit(0 if sys.argv[2] in fs else 1)' "$STATE/fs.json" "$1"; } # --- Refusal cases ---------------------------------------------------------- begin "Server refuses TLS" start_server notls; deploy "$WORK/home-trust"; stop_server check "deploy fails (rc=$RC)" failed check "client asked for TLS" log_has '^C: AUTH TLS' check "server never received USER or PASS" log_lacks '^C: (USER|PASS) ' check "nothing uploaded" log_lacks '^C: STOR ' check "password not in any output" pw_hidden end begin "Server certificate not trusted" start_server ok; deploy "$WORK/home-notrust"; stop_server check "deploy fails (rc=$RC)" failed check "lftp rejected the certificate" out_has 'Certificate verification' check "server never received PASS" log_lacks '^C: PASS ' check "nothing uploaded" log_lacks '^C: STOR ' check "password not in any output" pw_hidden end begin "Server rejects PROT P (cleartext data)" start_server noprot; deploy "$WORK/home-trust" --apply; stop_server check "deploy fails (rc=$RC)" failed check "script explains the PROT P refusal" out_has 'did not accept PROT P' check "no data connection was opened" log_lacks '^DATA ' check "nothing uploaded" log_lacks '^C: STOR ' check "password not in any output" pw_hidden end begin "Wrong password" start_server ok; T_PASS="wrong-password" deploy "$WORK/home-trust" --apply; stop_server check "deploy fails (rc=$RC)" failed check "script reports the login failure" out_has 'Could not log in' check "nothing uploaded" log_lacks '^C: STOR ' end # --- Success cases (one server, state carries over) ------------------------- start_server ok '{"/www/stale.html": "left over from an old upload"}' begin "Dry run on a fresh remote" deploy "$WORK/home-trust" check "deploy succeeds (rc=$RC)" succeeded check "TLS preflight passed" out_has 'TLS OK' check "summary: 5 new, 3 dirs" out_has 'Would change: 0 updated, 5 new, 0 deleted, 3 dirs created' check "summary lists the UTF-8 file name" out_has '+ jyväskylä.txt' check "nothing uploaded" log_lacks '^C: STOR ' check "everything after AUTH was encrypted" all_encrypted check "password not in any output" pw_hidden end begin "Dry run --delete" deploy "$WORK/home-trust" --delete check "deploy succeeds (rc=$RC)" succeeded check "summary: 1 deleted" out_has 'Would change: 0 updated, 5 new, 1 deleted' check "summary lists stale.html" out_has '- stale.html' check "stale.html still on the server" remote_has /www/stale.html end begin "Apply" deploy "$WORK/home-trust" --apply check "deploy succeeds (rc=$RC)" succeeded check "summary: 5 new" out_has 'Changed: 0 updated, 5 new, 0 deleted, 3 dirs created' check "index.html on the server" remote_has /www/index.html check "nested file on the server" remote_has /www/pdfs/agm.pdf check "UTF-8 file name on the server" remote_has '/www/jyväskylä.txt' check "stale.html kept (no --delete)" remote_has /www/stale.html check "every login and transfer encrypted" all_encrypted check "password not in any output" pw_hidden end begin "Rebuild with no content change" rebuild; before="$(stor_count)" deploy "$WORK/home-trust" --apply check "deploy succeeds (rc=$RC)" succeeded check "summary: nothing to do" out_has 'Nothing to do' check "no file re-uploaded" [ "$(stor_count)" -eq "$before" ] end begin "One file changed" rebuild; printf '

JCC

New season

\n' >"$FAKE/dist/index.html" deploy "$WORK/home-trust" check "deploy succeeds (rc=$RC)" succeeded check "summary: 1 updated, 0 new" out_has 'Would change: 1 updated, 0 new, 0 deleted' check "summary lists index.html as updated" out_has '~ index.html' end DE_LOCALE="$(locale -a 2>/dev/null | grep -iE '^de_DE\.utf-?8$' | head -n 1)" if [ -n "$DE_LOCALE" ]; then begin "German locale ($DE_LOCALE)" T_LC_ALL="$DE_LOCALE" T_LANG="$DE_LOCALE" deploy "$WORK/home-trust" check "deploy succeeds (rc=$RC)" succeeded check "summary still parsed: 1 updated" out_has 'Would change: 1 updated, 0 new, 0 deleted' end else echo "== German locale: SKIPPED (de_DE.UTF-8 not installed)" fi begin "--full treats every file as changed" rebuild deploy "$WORK/home-trust" --full check "deploy succeeds (rc=$RC)" succeeded check "summary: 5 updated" out_has 'Would change: 5 updated, 0 new, 0 deleted' end stop_server echo if [ "$FAILS" -eq 0 ]; then echo "All checks passed."; else echo "$FAILS check(s) FAILED."; exit 1; fi
